scope: Marsh entrance and plaza-facing low connecting-wing facade detail; no footprint, source terrain or campus expansion changes

observations: The large central pointed arch encloses a broad pale stone niche, with three substantially narrower dark lancets and smaller lower lights.
Two pointed door portals contain paired metal-framed doors. The two doors share a raised entrance stair with a central rail and solid stone side cheeks.
The front pinnacles have stepped stone profiles; the gable has a continuous shallow decorative band. Detailed heraldic sculpture is not resolved by this model.

changes: Replace the former full-width dark main-window field with an actual pierced inner stone niche and narrower three-light dark glazing. Keep the outer arch and fitted nave envelope.
Use a non-emissive, rough, non-metallic stained-glass finish locally, rather than the common blue reflective campus-glass treatment.
Model the paired entrance door frames and recessed panels; retain both existing portal apertures and threshold elevations.
Add flush step-front nosings, round central rails and stone side-cheek infill. Retain the eight existing 15 cm walking treads and the shared DEM apron.

Replace only plaza-facing low connector exterior wall triangles with perforated masonry and 26 cm recessed panes. Keep the original GIS collision ring, caps, other elevations and attached CAS boundary.
Use the shared granite paving style for the existing rose-coloured plaza finish. Its exact slab pattern remains an authored interpretation.
limits: Facade dimensions, fine tracery, door joinery and finial profiles are interpreted from one frontal photograph, not architectural survey measurements.
The v3 generated near-detail board supplies only a construction-quality target; it is not used as evidence of BU dimensions or ornament.
The existing window positions on STH/CAS and the low connector wings remain procedural. Only the visible depth hierarchy of the plaza-facing connector openings is changed.
No heraldic emblems, doorway sculpture, readable inscriptions or interiors are invented. Public navigation and the source DEM are unchanged.
